FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 25 *January 1985, after the draft finalized by the Dye Intermediates Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council.

0.2 4-Nitroy2-toluidine ( C,HsOsNs ) is an important dye intermediate. It is prepared by nitration of 2-toluidine sulphate and then hydrolysis. It is also commercially known as Fast Scarlet G Base. It is represented by the following stru~ctural formula:

"J"2

4-NITRO-2-TOL'UIDINE ( Moleclular Mass 152 )

0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same .as that of the specified value in this standard.

Add 5 g of potassium bromide and titrate When a drop of mixture from the against standard sodium nitrite. beaker is placed on starch iodide paper, instantaneously a blue ring is developed. Procedure

A-4.3.1 Preparation of the Chromatographic Plates - Mix 50 g of neutral silica gel with 85 to 90 ml of water for three minutes. Then, by means of the applicator, coat the plate with the silica gel layer of thickness not exceeding 0.25 mm and place it in the oven maintained at 110�C for By means of a needle, mark a thin line width wise on all 90 minutes. plates at about 3 cm from the upper edge. Also remove a band of about 5 mm width silica gel from either of the lateral sides of each plate.
*Methods for sampling and test for dye intermediates.

IS : 11177 - 1985 A-4.3.2 Preparation of the Sample a few minutes and weigh by material and transfer to a 100 ml and make up the solution to the methanol.
Solution - Homogenize the means of a weighing bottle volumetric flask. Dissolve mark by adding additional

sample for 4.0 g of the in methanol quantity of

A-4.3.3 Spot 10 ~1 of the sample solution ( A-4.3.2 ) and those of reference solutions of 5-nitro-2-toluidine ( A-4.2.1 ) on the thin layer plate. Place the developer in the chamber. Close the chamber with its lid and allow to achieve equilibrium. Now place the plate carefully in the chamber and allow the eluent to run in ascending manner for about 25 to 30 minutes. Remove the plate from the chamber and dry off the solvent in an air drier. Hold the plate for 20 seconds in nitrous acid fumes ( formed~by adding about 5 g of sodium nitrite to 50 ml of 5 N hydrochloric acid in a 5-litre beaker. Allow the plate to stand for 1 minute to remove excess nitrous fumes. Spray with 0.5 percent of methanolic solution of American base ( A-4.2.3 ). A-4.3.3.1 By visual comparison, the spot corresponding to 5-nitro-2toluidine in the sample shall have equal or less intensity than that of reference sample of 0.5 percent 5-nitro-2-toluidine and there shall be no other impurities on the thin layer glass plate.
